# Overview

Runs the Japanese extraction from CHILDES tokens through negation coding to `japanese_data/processed_data/japanese_tokens_processed.feather`. Uses `japanese` as the working directory with `childesr`, `tidyverse`, and `arrow`, requires `japanese_neg_lexicon.csv`, and reuses corpus caches unless `japanese_force_download` is `TRUE`.

# Setup

Loads `childesr`, `tidyverse`, and `arrow`, configures knitr, and creates `japanese_raw_dir` and `japanese_processed_dir`.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  error = FALSE,
  cache = FALSE
)
library(childesr)
library(tidyverse)
library(arrow)
```

```{r directories}
japanese_db_version <- "2026.1"
japanese_force_download <- FALSE

japanese_data_root <- "japanese_data"

japanese_raw_dir <- file.path(japanese_data_root, "raw_data")
japanese_processed_dir <- file.path(japanese_data_root, "processed_data")

# Hand-coded list of negation word forms (see the Negation rule document).
japanese_lexicon_path <- "japanese_neg_lexicon.csv"

dir.create(japanese_raw_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(japanese_processed_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

# Load Data

Selects CHILDES source corpora and imports tokens into `japanese_all_tokens` for annotation.

## Select Corpora

Selects the Japanese collection in `japanese_target_collection` for CHILDES release `japanese_db_version`.

```{r collections}
japanese_target_collection <- "Japanese"
```

## Import Data

Downloads or reuses corpus-level Japanese tokens in `japanese_all_tokens` and checks required columns and combined batch row counts.

```{r import_tokens}
# One folder for this DB version and query (all speakers, all tokens),
# one Feather file per corpus.
japanese_batch_dir <- file.path(
  japanese_raw_dir,
  paste0("corpus_batches_", japanese_db_version, "_all_speakers")
)

japanese_corpora_path <- file.path(japanese_batch_dir, "corpus_list.csv")
dir.create(japanese_batch_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Corpus list for the collection: fetched once, then reused from disk.
if (!japanese_force_download && file.exists(japanese_corpora_path)) {
  japanese_corpora_names <- readr::read_csv(
    japanese_corpora_path, show_col_types = FALSE
  )$corpus_name
} else {
  japanese_corpora_names <- childesr::get_corpora(db_version = japanese_db_version) %>%
    dplyr::filter(collection_name %in% japanese_target_collection) %>%
    dplyr::pull(corpus_name) %>%
    unique() %>%
    sort()
  if (length(japanese_corpora_names) == 0L) {
    stop("No corpora found for collection: ", japanese_target_collection)
  }
  readr::write_csv(
    tibble::tibble(corpus_name = japanese_corpora_names),
    japanese_corpora_path
  )
}

japanese_batch_files <- file.path(
  japanese_batch_dir,
  paste0(str_replace_all(japanese_corpora_names, "[^A-Za-z0-9_-]", "_"), ".feather")
)

# Columns every corpus file must have.
japanese_required_columns <- c(
  "target_child_id", "target_child_age", "transcript_id", "utterance_id",
  "token_order", "gloss", "part_of_speech", "speaker_role",
  "speaker_code", "utterance_type"
)

# A saved batch is usable if the file exists and has the required columns.
japanese_batch_is_valid <- function(path) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(FALSE)
  saved_columns <- names(arrow::open_dataset(path, format = "ipc"))
  all(japanese_required_columns %in% saved_columns)
}

# Write to a temporary file first, then rename it.
# If R stops mid-write, no half-written batch is left behind.
japanese_save_batch <- function(data, path) {
  temp_path <- paste0(path, ".tmp")
  arrow::write_feather(data, temp_path)
  if (!file.rename(temp_path, path)) stop("Could not save: ", path)
}

japanese_download_status <- tibble::tibble(
  corpus_name = japanese_corpora_names,
  status = "pending",
  n_tokens = NA_real_,
  error = NA_character_
)

for (i in seq_along(japanese_corpora_names)) {
  corpus_name <- japanese_corpora_names[[i]]
  path <- japanese_batch_files[[i]]
  message(sprintf("[%d/%d] %s", i, length(japanese_corpora_names), corpus_name))

  if (!japanese_force_download && japanese_batch_is_valid(path)) {
    # Already saved: reuse it and just count its rows.
    japanese_download_status$status[[i]] <- "cached"
    japanese_download_status$n_tokens[[i]] <-
      nrow(arrow::read_feather(path, col_select = "utterance_id"))

  } else {
    # Not saved yet: download all speakers (no role argument).
    # tryCatch turns an error into a message so the loop moves on.
    tokens <- tryCatch(
      childesr::get_tokens(
        corpus = corpus_name,
        token = "%",
        replace = TRUE,
        db_version = japanese_db_version
      ),
      error = function(e) conditionMessage(e)
    )

    if (is.character(tokens)) {
      # Download failed: tokens holds the error message.
      japanese_download_status$status[[i]] <- "failed"
      japanese_download_status$error[[i]] <- tokens
      message("  FAILED: ", tokens)
    } else if (is.null(tokens) || nrow(tokens) == 0L) {
      # Nothing returned: nothing to save, not counted as a failure.
      japanese_download_status$status[[i]] <- "empty"
      japanese_download_status$n_tokens[[i]] <- 0
      message("  No tokens returned.")
    } else if (!all(japanese_required_columns %in% names(tokens))) {
      japanese_download_status$status[[i]] <- "failed"
      japanese_download_status$error[[i]] <- paste(
        "Missing columns:",
        paste(setdiff(japanese_required_columns, names(tokens)), collapse = ", ")
      )
      message("  FAILED: ", japanese_download_status$error[[i]])
    } else {
      japanese_save_batch(tokens, path)
      japanese_download_status$status[[i]] <- "downloaded"
      japanese_download_status$n_tokens[[i]] <- nrow(tokens)
      message("  Saved ", nrow(tokens), " tokens.")
    }
  }
}

if (any(japanese_download_status$status == "failed")) {
  stop(
    "Some corpora failed. Completed batches remain saved. ",
    "Keep japanese_force_download <- FALSE and rerun this chunk."
  )
}

japanese_all_tokens <- japanese_batch_files[
  japanese_download_status$status %in% c("cached", "downloaded")
] %>%
  purrr::map(arrow::read_feather) %>%
  dplyr::bind_rows()

# The combined data should have exactly as many rows as the batches.
stopifnot(
  nrow(japanese_all_tokens) ==
    sum(japanese_download_status$n_tokens, na.rm = TRUE)
)

cat(sprintf(
  "Loaded %d tokens from %d children.\n",
  nrow(japanese_all_tokens),
  japanese_all_tokens$target_child_id %>% unique() %>% length()
))

japanese_download_status %>%
  dplyr::select(corpus_name, status, n_tokens)
```

# Token Processing

Filters `japanese_tokens` by `target_child_age` and assigns speaker, age, and utterance-type fields before negation coding.

## Filter Ages and Count Exclusions

Filters `japanese_all_tokens` to finite `target_child_age` values from 0 to under 72 months and records row and child counts in `japanese_exclusions`.

```{r exclusions}
japanese_n_tokens_before_exclusions <- nrow(japanese_all_tokens)
japanese_n_chi_before_exclusions <- japanese_all_tokens$target_child_id %>% unique() %>% length()

japanese_tokens <- japanese_all_tokens

japanese_tokens <- japanese_tokens %>%
  filter(is.finite(target_child_age))
japanese_n_tokens_after_finite_age <- nrow(japanese_tokens)
japanese_n_chi_after_finite_age <- japanese_tokens$target_child_id %>% unique() %>% length()

japanese_tokens <- japanese_tokens %>%
  filter(target_child_age >= 0, target_child_age < 72)
japanese_n_tokens_after_age_range <- nrow(japanese_tokens)
japanese_n_chi_after_age_range <- japanese_tokens$target_child_id %>% unique() %>% length()

japanese_exclusions <- tibble(
  n_tokens_before_exclusions = japanese_n_tokens_before_exclusions,
  n_after_finite_age = japanese_n_tokens_after_finite_age,
  n_after_age_range = japanese_n_tokens_after_age_range,
  missing_or_nonfinite_age =
    japanese_n_tokens_before_exclusions - japanese_n_tokens_after_finite_age,
  outside_age_range =
    japanese_n_tokens_after_finite_age - japanese_n_tokens_after_age_range,
  n_chi_total = japanese_n_chi_before_exclusions,
  n_chi_after_finite_age = japanese_n_chi_after_finite_age,
  n_chi_after_age_range = japanese_n_chi_after_age_range
)

japanese_exclusions
```

## Save Exclusion Records

Saves `japanese_exclusions` and the age-filtered `japanese_tokens` as CSV files in `japanese_raw_dir`.

```{r save_exclusions}
readr::write_csv(
  japanese_exclusions,
  file.path(japanese_raw_dir, "exclusions_japanese_summary.csv")
)
# Note: this file holds the tokens KEPT after the age exclusions.
readr::write_csv(
  japanese_tokens,
  file.path(japanese_raw_dir, "japanese_tokens_excluded.csv")
)
```

## Assign Speaker Roles

Maps target-child roles to `child` and other nonmissing roles to `parent` in `japanese_tokens$speaker`, leaving missing roles as `NA`.

```{r speaker_roles}
japanese_tokens <- japanese_tokens %>%
  mutate(
    speaker = if_else(
      str_to_lower(as.character(speaker_role), locale = "en") == "target_child",
      "child", "parent"
    )
  )
```

## Calculate Age in Months

Calculates `japanese_tokens$age` as the floor of `target_child_age` in months.

```{r age}
japanese_tokens$age <- japanese_tokens$target_child_age %>% floor()
```

## Recode Utterance Types

Recodes question, imperative, and disrupted labels from `utterance_type` into `japanese_tokens$utterance_type`, leaving unlisted values unchanged. Warns when any remaining label falls outside the four study categories.

```{r utterance_types}
# Prepare the utterance_type categories for this study based on the utterance_types in childes-db
## Categories: declarative, imperative, interrogative, and other
## Note: imperative_emphatic comes from the CHAT "!" terminator, which also marks exclamations.
japanese_tokens$utterance_type <-
  recode(japanese_tokens$utterance_type,
         question = "interrogative",
         `broken for coding` = "other",
         `imperative_emphatic` = "imperative",
         interruption = "other",
         `interruption question` = "interrogative",
         `missing CA terminator` = "other",
         `no break TCU continuation` = "other",
         `question exclamation` = "interrogative",
         `quotation next line` = "other",
         `quotation precedes` = "other",
         `self interruption` = "other",
         `self interruption question` = "interrogative",
         `trail off` = "other",
         `trail off question` = "interrogative"
  )

japanese_unlisted_types <- setdiff(
  unique(japanese_tokens$utterance_type),
  c("declarative", "imperative", "interrogative", "other")
)

if (length(japanese_unlisted_types) > 0L) {
  warning(
    "Utterance types left unchanged: ",
    paste(japanese_unlisted_types, collapse = ", ")
  )
}
```

# Define Target Words

Defines `nai` and `iya` targets with `japanese_neg_lexicon.csv` and labels matching tokens. Uses hand-coded forms because the available morphology fields do not reliably identify Japanese negatives.

- `nai`: the negative ending *-nai* whether written alone or attached (*nai*, *shiranai*, *tabenakatta*, *shinaide*, *kowaku nai*, *janai*).
- `iya`: *iya*, *iyada*, *yada*, *iyaiya*.
- `outside`: negation forms outside the target set, counted but not coded (*-masen*, *dame*, *chigau*, *uun*, *iie*).
- `exclude`: non-negating forms (*abunai*, *kamoshirenai*, *nainai*, *-nakya*, …).

## Load Negation Lexicon

Loads `japanese_neg_lexicon.csv` into `japanese_neg_lexicon` and validates its `form`, `target`, and `form_type` fields.

```{r load_lexicon}
japanese_normalize_gloss <- function(x) {
  x %>%
    as.character() %>%
    str_to_lower(locale = "en") %>%
    str_remove_all(":") %>%      # CHAT lengthening marks
    str_squish()
}

japanese_neg_lexicon <- readr::read_csv(japanese_lexicon_path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(form = japanese_normalize_gloss(form))

stopifnot(
  all(c("form", "target", "form_type") %in% names(japanese_neg_lexicon)),
  all(japanese_neg_lexicon$target %in% c("nai", "iya", "outside", "exclude")),
  !anyDuplicated(japanese_neg_lexicon$form)
)

count(japanese_neg_lexicon, target)
```

## Match Target Forms

Joins normalized token glosses to `japanese_neg_lexicon` and reports negative-looking forms missing from the lexicon in `japanese_uncoded`.

```{r match_lexicon}
japanese_n_before_join <- nrow(japanese_tokens)

japanese_tokens <- japanese_tokens %>%
  mutate(gloss_norm = japanese_normalize_gloss(gloss)) %>%
  left_join(
    japanese_neg_lexicon %>% select(form, lex_target = target, neg_form = form_type),
    by = c("gloss_norm" = "form")
  )

stopifnot(nrow(japanese_tokens) == japanese_n_before_join)

japanese_candidate_pattern <-
  "(nai|nakatta|nakute|naide|nakya|nakucha|nakereba|masen|ない|ナイ)$|^(iya|yada|いや|イヤ|やだ)"

japanese_uncoded <- japanese_tokens %>%
  filter(is.na(lex_target), str_detect(gloss_norm, japanese_candidate_pattern)) %>%
  count(gloss_norm, speaker) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = speaker, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)

if (nrow(japanese_uncoded) > 0L) {
  warning(
    nrow(japanese_uncoded),
    " negative-looking forms are not in the lexicon and were treated as nonfunction. ",
    "See japanese_uncoded and add them to ", japanese_lexicon_path, "."
  )
}
```

## Apply Context Exclusions

Flags `shika ... nai`, obligation forms, `nan demo nai`, and baby-talk sequences in `japanese_tokens$context_exclusion`.

```{r context_exclusions}
japanese_obligation_pattern <- "(nakya|nakucha|nakereba)$"
japanese_obligation_completers <- c("ikenai", "naranai", "dame", "ikemasen", "narimasen")

# Gloss k positions away (k = 1 previous, k = 2 two back, k = -1 next, ...),
# or "" when that position is outside the table or in a different utterance.
japanese_neighbour <- function(x, utt, k) {
  i <- seq_along(x) - k
  ok <- i >= 1L & i <= length(x)
  ok[ok] <- utt[i[ok]] == utt[ok]
  out <- rep("", length(x))
  out[ok] <- x[i[ok]]
  out
}

japanese_tokens <- japanese_tokens %>%
  arrange(utterance_id, token_order)

japanese_tokens$context_exclusion <- local({
  g      <- coalesce(japanese_tokens$gloss_norm, "")
  utt    <- japanese_tokens$utterance_id
  n      <- length(g)
  idx    <- seq_len(n)
  is_nai <- japanese_tokens$lex_target %in% "nai"

  prev1 <- japanese_neighbour(g, utt, 1L)
  prev2 <- japanese_neighbour(g, utt, 2L)
  next1 <- japanese_neighbour(g, utt, -1L)
  next2 <- japanese_neighbour(g, utt, -2L)

  # Row on which each utterance starts (rows are sorted by utterance).
  utt_start <- cummax(if_else(c(TRUE, utt[-1] != utt[-n]), idx, 0L))

  # Last "shika" and last nai-type negator strictly before each row, across
  # the whole table. A "shika" only counts if it lies in the current
  # utterance (position >= utt_start).
  last_shika <- c(0L, cummax(if_else(g == "shika", idx, 0L))[-n])
  last_nai   <- c(0L, cummax(if_else(is_nai, idx, 0L))[-n])

  case_when(
    is_nai & last_shika >= utt_start & last_shika > last_nai ~
      "shika_nai",
    g == "nai" & ((prev1 == "demo" & prev2 == "nan") | prev1 == "nandemo") ~
      "nan_demo_nai",
    g %in% japanese_obligation_completers &
      (str_detect(prev1, japanese_obligation_pattern) |
         (prev1 == "wa" & str_detect(prev2, "nakute$"))) ~
      "obligation",
    is_nai & str_detect(g, "nakute$") & next1 == "wa" &
      next2 %in% japanese_obligation_completers ~
      "obligation",
    g == "nai" & (prev1 == "nai" | next1 == "nai") ~
      "baby_talk",
    g == "inai" & (prev1 == "inai" | next1 %in% c("inai", "baa")) ~
      "baby_talk",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )
})
```

## Assign Target Word Labels

Assigns `nai` or `iya` to `japanese_tokens$word` for targets without context exclusions and records other reasons in `neg_exclusion_reason`.

```{r function_words}
japanese_tokens <- japanese_tokens %>%
  mutate(
    neg_exclusion_reason = case_when(
      lex_target == "exclude" ~ paste0("lexicon: ", neg_form),
      lex_target == "outside" ~ "outside target set",
      lex_target %in% c("nai", "iya") & !is.na(context_exclusion) ~
        paste0("context: ", context_exclusion),
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    word = if_else(
      lex_target %in% c("nai", "iya") & is.na(context_exclusion),
      lex_target,
      "nonfunction"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(-context_exclusion)
```

## Assign Word Categories

Assigns `Negation` to matched targets and `nonfunction` to other rows in `japanese_tokens$word_category`.

```{r wordcategories}
japanese_tokens$word_category <- "nonfunction"
japanese_tokens$word_category[japanese_tokens$word %in% c("nai", "iya")] <- "Negation"
```

## Assign Syntactic Categories

Assigns `Function` to negation targets and `nonfunction` to other rows in `japanese_tokens$syncategory`.

```{r syncategory}
japanese_tokens$syncategory <- "Function"
japanese_tokens$syncategory[japanese_tokens$word_category == "nonfunction"] <- "nonfunction"
```

# Classify Negation

Normalizes included target labels and classifies their scope using utterance context in `japanese_tokens`.

## Normalize Negation Categories

Copies included `nai` and `iya` labels from `word` into `japanese_tokens$negation_category`.

```{r negation_clean}
japanese_tokens <- japanese_tokens %>%
  mutate(
    negation_category = if_else(word %in% c("nai", "iya"), word, NA_character_)
  )
```

## Assign Negation Scope

Assigns `discourse` or `sentential` in `japanese_tokens$negation_scope` using negator position, repetitions, and surrounding particles or fillers.

- **Discourse:** the negator stands alone — bare (*nai!*, *iya!*), a single negated verb or adjective (*iranai*, *kowaku nai*), *moo nai*, a repetition (*iya iya*), or *iya* followed by a new clause.
- **Sentential:** other content comes before the negator, or anything follows it (*omocha ga nai*, *inu janai*, *nai kara*).

```{r negation_categorization}
japanese_final_particles <- c("no", "ne", "yo", "wa", "na", "sa", "desu")
japanese_leading_ignorable <- c("ee", "a", "ano", "moo")

japanese_assign_scope <- function(g, target, in_core) {
  scope <- rep(NA_character_, length(g))
  core_idx <- which(in_core)

  for (i in which(!is.na(target))) {
    before_idx <- core_idx[core_idx < i]
    after_idx <- core_idx[core_idx > i]

    if (target[i] == "iya") {
      # iya first (or only preceded by other iya forms) is discourse,
      # whatever follows it ("iya, kore ga ii").
      first_or_repeat <- all(target[before_idx] %in% "iya")
      scope[i] <- if (first_or_repeat) "discourse" else "sentential"
    } else {
      # nai must stand alone: nothing after it except repeats, and nothing
      # before it except repeats or one adjective in -ku ("kowaku nai").
      same_before <- all(g[before_idx] == g[i])
      same_after <- all(g[after_idx] == g[i])
      adjective_before <- length(before_idx) == 1L && g[i] == "nai" &&
        str_detect(g[before_idx], "ku$")
      scope[i] <- if ((same_before || adjective_before) && same_after) {
        "discourse"
      } else {
        "sentential"
      }
    }
  }
  scope
}

japanese_neg_utterances <- japanese_tokens %>%
  filter(!is.na(negation_category)) %>%
  distinct(utterance_id)

japanese_scope <- japanese_tokens %>%
  semi_join(japanese_neg_utterances, by = "utterance_id") %>%
  arrange(utterance_id, token_order) %>%
  group_by(utterance_id) %>%
  mutate(
    .g = coalesce(gloss_norm, ""),
    .lead = cumall(.g %in% japanese_leading_ignorable),
    .trail = rev(cumall(rev(.g %in% japanese_final_particles))),
    negation_scope = japanese_assign_scope(.g, negation_category, !.lead & !.trail)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(utterance_id, token_order, negation_scope)

japanese_tokens <- japanese_tokens %>%
  select(-any_of(c("negation_scope", "utterance_negation_scope", "neg_type"))) %>%
  left_join(japanese_scope, by = c("utterance_id", "token_order"))

stopifnot(
  nrow(japanese_tokens) == japanese_n_before_join,
  all(!is.na(japanese_tokens$negation_scope[!is.na(japanese_tokens$negation_category)]))
)
```

# Save Processed Data

Saves `japanese_tokens` to `japanese_data/processed_data/japanese_tokens_processed.feather` for downstream counts and plots.

```{r save_processed_data}
write_feather(
  japanese_tokens,
  file.path(japanese_processed_dir, "japanese_tokens_processed.feather")
)
```
